The blood and serological tests showed an increase in C-reactive protein concentration (3.58 mg/dL) in the absence of leukocytosis and with a normal platelet count (180,000/mm3). The examination of the peripheral smear showed the presence of some large mononuclear elements with hyperbasophile cytoplasm. No alterations in platelet morphology were evidenced.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 15-month-old girl developed petechiae on the soft palate and a progressive hemorrhagic rash on limbs, face, and auricles, accompanied by strong edema and a moderate fever following recent MMR vaccination and a mild febrile diarrhea. Initial platelet counts were normal, excluding immune thrombocytopenic purpura. Inflammatory markers showed elevated CRP without leukocytosis; peripheral smear revealed large mononuclear cells without platelet abnormalities. Ultrasound excluded visceral involvement. During hospitalization, bilateral metacarpophalangeal joint edema and pain appeared, resolving with analgesics within a week. Although skin biopsy histopathology was not documented, clinical presentation, laboratory findings, and course supported the diagnosis of AHEI.

Bilateral metacarpophalangeal joint edema and pain resolving with analgesics within a week
